paragraphs: The union uses same-page greedy one-to-one matching at normalized title similarity ≥0.90. It strips HTML, normalizes Unicode and alphanumeric text, and uses SequenceMatcher with autojunk=False. Matched source candidates are deduplicated; unmatched candidates are merged while preserving relative order. This operates on parser outputs, not gold labels.

sections.title: Prompt and decoding
paragraphs: The same PROMPT is used for each report. It asks for logical hierarchy, treats executive summaries/main sections/annexes as top level, rejects captions, table cells, running headers, emphasis and TOC entries, and requires consistent parallel sections. The decoder strips a code-fence wrapper, then validates every ID and value. Accepted IDs are joined back to their original titles and pages; null rejects a candidate. A missing source title cannot be created by this method. Invalid responses are recorded as errors and yield no accepted headings for that document.

sections.title: What each model learns
paragraphs: The 33 measurements of selectable PDF text lines cover font size relative to document body text, font-size rank, bold/italic proportions, RGB color, normalized position/width/height, gaps, adjacent-line style/block indicators, repeated-text count, log character/word counts, uppercase/digit fractions, numeric-prefix depth, number-only lines, dot leaders, sentence endings and a generic multilingual caption-prefix indicator. The relationship classifier uses 142 features: two 47-feature groups, their differences and page delta. Its 867 training pairs are consecutive annotated headings. Target −1 means the next H number is smaller (shallower), 0 means equal and +1 means larger (deeper). It learns direction, not the number of levels skipped.

sections.title: Sequence decoding
paragraphs: First, choosing the highest body-or-heading score decides which predicted groups survive. Viterbi then maximizes the sum of log heading-class probabilities and weighted log relationship probabilities for transitions between retained groups. Transition class is sign(next H − previous H); probabilities are clipped below at 1e-12. Default relation weight is 1.0. This decoder is an algorithm, not a fourth trained model, and cannot recover a group already rejected as body.

sections.title: Selection, not a tree-parameter search
paragraphs: We compared three pipeline variants, with identical fixed tree settings. F1 = 2 × exact group-and-level matches / (gold groups + predicted groups); group matching requires identical source-line membership.

The original separate 38-heading v2 test achieved 85.7% exact group-and-level F1: 38 matched groups, 36 correctly leveled and 8 additional false groups. That small test is distinct from the historical 77-heading table.

sections.title: Deployment and timing

sections.title: How to interpret this result
paragraphs: The model emitted 50 headings and 36 had both the correct title and level. Its one extra heading should not hide the 28 missing reference headings. The 65.0% score is lower than the recorded Chandra configuration’s 72.6%, while measured processing time is shorter. Backend and pipeline differences prevent attributing that difference solely to the weights.

sections.title: Which components were trained
paragraphs: The main model, vision projector and DSpark draft are upstream published models. We did not train or fine-tune them. Q8_0 stores the main and draft weights in an 8-bit quantized format; the projector stays in F16. This differs from the earlier original-BF16 run.

sections.title: What this rerun establishes
paragraphs: Running the full official package on its documented Mac deployment did not improve the heading-level counts. Its native formatter still disagrees with our reference hierarchy. This result describes the complete configuration and does not isolate the recognition weights from layout and assembly.

The package queues crops across the sample. Our measured time is for all 32 pages; the table’s per-page time is that total divided by 32, not a claim that each individual page completed in 14.56 seconds.

xiaomi_ocr0_official_metal.family: Two-stage OCR · CPU layout and Metal recognition
xiaomi_ocr0_official_metal.summary: Xiaomi’s upstream two-stage pipeline uses native PaddleX layout on CPU and BF16 recognition through vLLM Metal. Its default formatter assigns paragraph titles H2.

stages.title: Render each audited PDF page
stages.detail: Render the same 32 physical pages at 200 DPI in RGB. No native PDF text, document tags or reference headings enter inference.

stages.title: Locate text, titles, tables and formulas
stages.detail: Run native PP-DocLayoutV3 through PaddleX on CPU with the published benchmark threshold 0.25. Xiaomi’s upstream serializer preserves the detected regions and reading order.

stages.title: Recognize each crop with Xiaomi-OCR-0
stages.detail: The unchanged upstream CLI sends one region at a time to vLLM Metal. Original BF16 weights receive the official text, formula or table prompt; tables use Xiaomi’s structured table tokens.

stages.title: Apply the upstream retry and assembly code
stages.detail: Use the official repetition retry policy, then convert formulas and tables and assemble the page. The default title_profile="v2" makes document titles H1 and paragraph titles H2. No retry was triggered across these 32 pages.

sections.title: What changed from the earlier Xiaomi row
paragraphs: The earlier trial sent each complete page directly to Xiaomi through MLX. This run uses the upstream layout, crop recognition, table conversion and page assembly pipeline. Correct title-level pairs increase from 29 to 31 out of 77; joint F0.5 increases from 39.7% to 42.9%.
The pipeline remains adapted to this Mac: layout uses CPU, and recognition uses vLLM Metal instead of the documented CUDA servers. The model weights and upstream recognition/assembly code are pinned.

sections.title: Why the heading levels are limited
paragraphs: We executed the upstream paragraph-title formatter on “# Introduction”, “### Methods” and “1.1 Features”. It returned H2 for all three. In the actual mid-term report, page 26, both “1. Introduction” and “1.1 EVALUATION FEATURES” are H2. The ordinary paragraph beginning “3. The MTE’s key features are” is also emitted as H2.
The saved region field named merged has already passed through assembly. It is not an untouched model response. We therefore do not claim the recognition model itself chose every reported level.

sections.title: What the timing includes
paragraphs: Measured total: 7 min 52 sec for 32 pages, averaging 14.8 seconds per page. Includes rendering, CPU layout, launching the upstream command separately for each page, recognition, assembly and saving. CPU layout initialization took a separate 2.0 seconds; recognition weights were already loaded after the cover smoke test.

All 32 pages completed without reported recognition failures. The upstream retry reports show zero repetition retries. Complete per-request finish reasons are unavailable, so token-limit hits are not reported as zero. Only this OCR model was running; unrelated host workloads were not controlled.

evidencelab.family: Full document parser · isolated Docker · CPU
evidencelab.summary: EvidenceLab combines Docling 2.58.0 with a hierarchical post-processor, font and numbering rules, and final contents-list normalization. We score that final list exactly as returned.

stages.title: Parse the full PDF with Docling
stages.detail: Docling 2.58.0 uses Heron layout detection and TableFormer fast. OCR is disabled. The isolated Linux ARM64 container has four CPU cores and a 12 GB memory limit.

stages.title: Run EvidenceLab’s hierarchy processing
stages.detail: docling-hierarchical-pdf 0.1.2 assigns levels from PDF hierarchy metadata when available, otherwise from heading geometry and font style. EvidenceLab applies its built-in safeguards afterward.

stages.title: Keep the final contents list
stages.detail: EvidenceLab creates and normalizes toc.txt, including front matter and numbered sections. We preserve its H levels and 80-character title limit.

evidencelab.limitation: 37/77 heading-level pairs are correct. There are 26 matched headings at the wrong level, 14 missing headings and 7 extra headings. This is not a complete, accurate outline.

sections.title: Training and selection
paragraphs: No WFP-specific training or setting search was performed. This configuration reproduces the parser and post-processing in the running EvidenceLab image. It uses an older Docling release than our Docling-only rows, so the difference cannot be attributed to post-processing alone.

sections.title: Reproducibility
paragraphs: The runner calls ParseProcessor.process_document without a database. The image digest, source revision, model revisions, file hashes, native headings, full-PDF timings and archived runner hash are recorded. Repeated runs download the recorded model revisions before switching Hugging Face to offline mode.

sections.title: Training and selection
paragraphs: No models were trained or tuned on WFP reports for this configuration. Latin-script recognition was selected to cover the English and Spanish documents. The earlier Docling configurations explicitly disabled OCR.

sections.title: Interpretation
paragraphs: This tests forced full-page OCR on PDFs with selectable text. It does not measure performance on a scanned-document corpus, and it is not an exhaustive comparison of Docling’s OCR engines.

sections.title: Observed outputs
paragraphs: The 69 audit predictions comprise 5 H1, 13 H2, 9 H3, 9 H4, 23 H5 and 10 H6 headings. Of 67 matched titles, 52 have the wrong level. Native prose retention is 86.6% on the audit pages. This is a text-retention measure, not a character-accuracy score.
